name: Papyrus 1 (P.Oxy. 2)
summary: A single leaf from a papyrus codex found at Oxyrhynchus in 1896–97 by Grenfell and Hunt — the earliest surviving copy of Matthew's genealogy, with the sacred names written as abbreviations (nomina sacra).

media.caption: 𝔓1 recto: Matthew 1:1–9, 12. The title-like first line reads ΒΙΒΛΟΣ ΓΕΝΕΣΕΩΣ ΙΥ ΧΥ.

sources.title: B. P. Grenfell & A. S. Hunt, The Oxyrhynchus Papyri, Part I (1898), no. 2

name: Rylands Papyrus 457
summary: A credit-card-sized scrap of John's trial narrative, usually cited as the oldest surviving New Testament manuscript. Its date rests on handwriting comparison alone, so estimates range from the early second to the early third century.

sources.title: C. H. Roberts, An Unpublished Fragment of the Fourth Gospel in the John Rylands Library (1935)
'The Use and Abuse of P52: Papyrological Pitfalls in the Dating of the Fourth Gospel'
sources.author: Brent Nongbri
sources.note: Harvard Theological Review 98 — argues the palaeographic range is wider than often claimed

name: P.Oxy. 4404
summary: A fragment of the parable of the tenants, among the earliest witnesses to Matthew; it lacks 21:44, which some manuscripts include.

sources.title: J. D. Thomas, The Oxyrhynchus Papyri, vol. 64 (1997), no. 4404

name: Chester Beatty Papyrus I
held: Chester Beatty Library, Dublin (and Vienna, P.Vindob. G 31974)
summary: The earliest codex to contain all four Gospels and Acts together, though only about 30 leaves of some 220 survive.

sources.title: F. G. Kenyon, The Chester Beatty Biblical Papyri, fasc. II (1933–34)

name: Chester Beatty Papyrus II
held: Chester Beatty Library, Dublin; University of Michigan
summary: The earliest collection of Paul's letters, with Hebrews placed right after Romans. 86 of the original 104 leaves survive.

sources.title: F. G. Kenyon, The Chester Beatty Biblical Papyri, fasc. III (1936)

name: Bodmer Papyrus II
summary: A nearly complete early codex of John, corrected by the scribe himself in hundreds of places.

sources.title: V. Martin, Papyrus Bodmer II (1956; supplement 1962)

name: Bodmer Papyri XIV–XV
summary: Luke and John in one codex, textually very close to Codex Vaticanus of a century later — evidence that the 'Alexandrian' text was copied carefully over long periods.

sources.title: V. Martin & R. Kasser, Papyrus Bodmer XIV–XV (1961)

name: Codex Sinaiticus
held: British Library, London (with leaves in Leipzig, St Petersburg and St Catherine's, Sinai)
summary: The oldest complete New Testament, on parchment, found by Tischendorf at St Catherine's Monastery in 1844–59. It ends Mark at 16:8 and lacks John 7:53–8:11. Fully digitised online.

name: Codex Vaticanus
summary: In the Vatican since at least 1475; with Sinaiticus the chief witness to the early Alexandrian text. Digitised by the Vatican Library.

name: The Great Isaiah Scroll
held: Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem
summary: All 66 chapters of Isaiah on 17 sheets of leather, found in Qumran Cave 1 in 1947 — a thousand years older than the previously oldest complete Hebrew Isaiah, and substantially the same text.

sources.title: M. Burrows, The Dead Sea Scrolls of St. Mark's Monastery, vol. 1 (1950)
Digital Dead Sea Scrolls (Israel Museum / Google)

name: Nash Papyrus
summary: The Ten Commandments followed by the Shema, on a single sheet bought in Egypt in 1902 — before the Dead Sea Scrolls, the oldest known Hebrew biblical text. Probably a liturgical or teaching sheet rather than a Bible.

sources.title: S. A. Cook, 'A Pre-Massoretic Biblical Papyrus', PSBA 25 (1903)

name: Ketef Hinnom silver amulets
summary: Two rolled silver strips inscribed with the priestly blessing, the oldest known extract of any biblical text. See the Insights card on Numbers 6.

sources.title: G. Barkay et al., 'The Amulets from Ketef Hinnom', BASOR 334 (2004)

name: 4Q51 Samuel
summary: Fragments of Samuel from Qumran Cave 4 that often agree with the Septuagint against the Masoretic text, and preserve a paragraph about Nahash the Ammonite before 1 Samuel 11 that is missing from the traditional Hebrew.

sources.title: F. M. Cross et al., Discoveries in the Judaean Desert XVII: Qumran Cave 4.XII, 1–2 Samuel (2005)
